worked: Married filing combined (joint federal), ages 45 and 43. Two equal earners: the case that shows the largest gap between the projection's one chart and the form's two. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 91,500.00 = 91,500.00. Federal taxable income = 91,500.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 60,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 91,500.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 91,500.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 91,500.00 - 0.00 = 91,500.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 0.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 26 subtotal 91,500.00 - 0.00 - 31,500.00 = 60,000.00. Line 29 taxable income 60,000.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 1,313.00 = 32.825 + 3% x 1,313.00 = 39.39 + 3.5% x 1,313.00 = 45.955 + 4% x 1,313.00 = 52.52 + 4.5% x 1,313.00 = 59.085 + 4.7% x 50,809.00 = 2388.023; total 2644.058 = 2,644.06. The form itself splits this: Line 5 Y 45,750.00, S 45,750.00; Line 7 50% / 50%; Line 27 30,000.00 and 30,000.00; Lines 30Y and 30S 1234 + 1234 = 2468 on Line 36. The projection applies the chart once to the couple's total, so expected is 2,644.06. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 91,500.00 - Line 8 0.00 = 91,500.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 91,500.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).

Married filing combined: Missouri figures a separate tax for each spouse on that spouse's share of taxable income, using the one chart twice, and this is required, not chosen. The projection applies the chart once to the couple's total taxable income, because the format has no way to say tax is per spouse.
